title: Yosi bar Menashya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah chapter 3, at the end of halakhah 2, the names are given as “R' Hinena, R' Pinekh, Rav Matna, Yosi bar Menashya, in the name of Rav.” In [Megillah chapter 2, halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.2.4.4), the wording is “R' Helbo, Rav Yosi bar Minisha, in the name of Rav.” It is possible that he is the one called in the Babylonian Talmud Rav Yosi son of Rav Menashya of Dewil, who was a student of Rav, as in [Kiddushin 79b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.79b.7) and [Niddah 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.26b.10).[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman gives Sukkah 3:2. The chain is at [Sukkah 3:1:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.3.1.8), with Rabbi Parnakh in the place of Hyman’s Pinekh. Megillah 2:4 gives Rav Matna between Rabbi Helbo and Yosi and spells Yosi’s patronymic two ways. Compare [Moed Katan 3:7:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.7.14) and [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1973&lang=en).
The consulted Kiddushin and Niddah passages name Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya of Dewil. Hyman gives Rav Yosi and suggests a possible identification.
